raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--tool-call-parser deepseekv3` and `tools` in the request, a streamed answer loses every ``` in its normal content, while the same answer without streaming keeps them. Code blocks in DeepSeek-V3, V3-0324 and R1-0528 answers arrive at the client as bare text: `json\n{...}\n` instead of a fenced block. Clients that send tools and stream, as most coding agents do, hit this on every answer that contains code. `--tool-call-parser auto` also picks `deepseekv3` for these templates.

`DeepSeekV3Detector.parse_streaming_increment` strips `"```"` from any text that has no tool-call marker (`deepseekv3_detector.py:104`). `detect_and_parse` (non-streaming) does not strip it, and `DeepSeekV31Detector` leaves fences alone in the same branch.

Repro (one token per delta, the default `--stream-interval 1`):

```
non-stream: 'Here is an example:\n```json\n{"a": 1, "b": [2]}\n```\nDone.'
stream    : 'Here is an example:\njson\n{"a": 1, "b": [2]}\n\nDone.'
```

## Modifications

- `deepseekv3_detector.py`: stop removing `"```"` from normal text in `parse_streaming_increment`. The EOS and `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` tokens are still removed.
- Why the strip existed: `"```"` was added in #5592, when the partial call regex did not require the closing fence and the buffer was cleared before the fence arrived. #7562 made the regex require the closing fence, so since then the strip has only removed fences from user answers.
- The fences around tool-call arguments never reach this branch: the call regex needs the closing fence before it matches, and the completed call is then cut from the buffer. This change does not alter tool-call output; the only difference from main is the restored fences in prose.
- Three unit tests in `TestDeepSeekV3Detector`:
  - a fenced prose answer streamed token by token matches the non-streaming result;
  - a fenced answer followed by a tool call keeps the fence and still parses the call and its arguments;
  - a multi-token delta carrying the closing fence and `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` (as with MTP or `--stream-interval` above 1) adds no normal text.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: parser change only, no model forward code. No GPU or end-to-end server run.

Unit tests, run on CPU (WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64, Python 3.12):
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`: 253 passed on this branch (250 existing + 3 new).
- The two fence tests fail with main's detector (fences are stripped from the normal text); the multi-token guard passes on both.
- An ad-hoc comparison of main's and this branch's detector over 8,560 delta splits (one token per delta, fixed and random multi-token groups, character splits) of 10 scenarios, including back-to-back calls and fences inside arguments, found identical tool-call output and no fence from tool-call syntax in normal text. Not committed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No docs describe this behavior.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable (parser string handling).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -1562,6 +1562,115 @@ def test_parse_streaming_multiple_tool_calls_with_multi_token_chunk(self):
         self.assertEqual(params1["city"], "Shanghai")
         self.assertEqual(params2["city"], "Beijing")
 
+    def test_parse_streaming_keeps_code_fences_in_normal_text(self):
+        """Code fences in a plain answer survive streaming, as they do in non-streaming."""
+        text = 'Here is an example:\n```json\n{"a": 1}\n```\nDone.'
+        chunks = [
+            "Here",
+            " is",
+            " an",
+            " example",
+            ":\n",
+            "```",
+            "json",
+            "\n",
+            '{"',
+            "a",
+            '":',
+            " ",
+            "1",
+            "}\n",
+            "```\n",
+            "Done",
+            ".",
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual("".join(chunks), text)
+
+        streamed = ""
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = self.detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            self.assertEqual(result.calls, [])
+            streamed += result.normal_text
+
+        self.assertEqual(streamed, text)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            DeepSeekV3Detector().detect_and_parse(text, self.tools).normal_text, text
+        )
+
+    def test_parse_streaming_code_fence_then_tool_call(self):
+        """A fenced answer followed by a tool call keeps the fence and parses the call."""
+        chunks = [
+            "Run",
+            " this",
+            ":\n",
+            "```",
+            "python",
+            "\n",
+            "print",
+            "(1)",
+            "\n",
+            "```\n",
+            "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>",
+            "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>",
+            "function",
+            "<｜tool▁sep｜>",
+            "get",
+            "_weather",
+            "\n",
+            "```",
+            "json",
+            "\n",
+            '{"',
+            "city",
+            '":',
+            ' "',
+            "Paris",
+            '"}',
+            "\n",
+            "```",
+            "<｜tool▁call▁end｜>",
+            "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>",
+        ]
+
+        normal_text = ""
+        names = []
+        arguments = ""
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = self.detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            normal_text += result.normal_text
+            for call in result.calls:
+                if call.name:
+                    names.append(call.name)
+                arguments += call.parameters or ""
+
+        self.assertEqual(normal_text, "Run this:\n```python\nprint(1)\n```\n")
+        self.assertEqual(names, ["get_weather"])
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(arguments), {"city": "Paris"})
+
+    def test_parse_streaming_multi_token_call_end_emits_no_fence(self):
+        """A delta with the closing fence and the call-end token adds no normal text."""
+        chunks = [
+            "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n```json\n",
+            '{"city": "Paris"}',
+            "\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>",
+            "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>",
+        ]
+
+        normal_text = ""
+        names = []
+        arguments = ""
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = self.detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            normal_text += result.normal_text
+            for call in result.calls:
+                if call.name:
+                    names.append(call.name)
+                arguments += call.parameters or ""
+
+        self.assertEqual(normal_text, "")
+        self.assertEqual(names, ["get_weather"])
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(arguments), {"city": "Paris"})
+
